answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked until it completes a useful task and survives a random audit. Auditors compare its work with a mirror of prior submissions and flag clusters that share unusual errors; a ridge of repeated links can trigger a deeper review. The harbor is a small, capped community pool that pays for audits, not a promise of perfect detection. A sybil operator must tie up capital for every identity and risks losing bonds when copied work or coordinated behavior is exposed.
